title: Carry a datum line's height to a far post with a reservoir water level, holding the jar on the line to mark
instruction: Use the water level to mark the height of the datum post's black line on the far post with the red marker, then put the jar and the hose end back in their stands.
context: Carpenters (O*NET 47-2031.00) carry a height around a room or a site with a water level, to set a ledger, a deck or a line of cabinets on one datum when the floor is not level and the far point is out of sight of a spirit level (Fine Homebuilding, "Making and Using Water Levels", 1994). In a reservoir water level the water in the jar and in the clear end tube stands at one height, and because the jar is far wider, the water follows the jar: its water is held on the datum line, by hand where there is nothing to stand it on, while the far end's water surface is marked. The far end must be raised before the jar goes up and the jar lowered before the end comes down, or water runs out of the end's mouth. Here the far post stands on a 2.5 cm pad, so copying the line's height above the floor is 2.5 cm off; 1.5 mm (a sixteenth of an inch) is the working tolerance.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. Datum post (fixed): pine, 4 by 4 cm, 18 cm tall, centered at (30, 23.5), a black datum line 2 mm wide painted all round at 13.0 cm. Far post (fixed): pine, 4 by 4 cm, centered at (30, -23.5), standing on a gray pad 12 by 12 by 2.5 cm, top at 18 cm; a plywood shelf on its inboard face, floor at 4 cm with a 1 cm rim on three sides, 5.2 by 5.6 cm inside; a red sliding marker on its front face, held by friction, with a grip tab 4.5 by 2.4 by 2 cm sticking out toward the robot from its outboard half (8 mm off center) and a thin pointer reaching in front of a tube standing on the shelf; the pointer's top edge is the mark, at 9.2 cm at the start. Water level: a clear round plastic jar 10 cm across and 10 cm tall (9.4 cm inside) with a vented lid and a black carry handle across it (a bar 5 by 2.5 cm, 3 cm tall), 150 g, standing in a plywood tray (1 cm rim, 12 cm square inside) centered at (22, 14); 1.2 m of 3/8 inch bore clear vinyl hose from a fitting in the jar's bottom, coiled on the table at (22, 0); the hose end: a clear acrylic tube (12.7 mm bore, 9 cm long, from 3 to 12 cm above the stick's bottom) taped to the front face of a pine stick 2.5 by 2.5 by 15 cm on a 4 by 4 cm foot, 80 g, standing in a tray (8 cm square inside) centered at (22, -14). Blue-tinted water stands 6 cm above the table in both with both in their trays. To build it: a 1 L clear jar with a bulkhead hose fitting in its bottom, clear vinyl tubing and an acrylic tube taped to a stick (reservoir-type water levels are sold the same way: a jug on a long clear hose with a clear end tube), two pine posts, a 2.5 cm board for the pad, a small rimmed shelf screwed to the far post, and a stiff red plastic clip with a tab and a pointer for the marker.
scoring: 0 if more than 1 mL spills at any point (a mouth below the water: the end left in its tray or put back while the jar is up, the jar tipped) or the hose is pulled taut. The marker counts as moved once its edge is more than 0.5 mm from where it was last counted; its last move must be a transfer: the jar within 3 cm of its spot 1 cm off the datum post, within 15 degrees of upright, gripped by its handle by a hand not on the marker, its water within 1.5 mm of the line; the end's tube within 2.5 cm of its spot behind the pointer, within 15 degrees of upright; the marker's edge within 1.5 mm of the end's water. At the end the jar and the end stand back in their trays (within 2.5 cm, bottom within 5 mm of the table, upright within 10 degrees, still, every tool point and pad tip 1 cm clear) and the marker is let go. Then the mark within 1.5 mm (a sixteenth of an inch) of the datum height with both arms home and still = 1.0 (0.9 if not home); otherwise 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.9, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held 1 s. Real trial: measure the mark and the line from a laser line to 0.5 mm with a steel rule, weigh the level before and after (1 g = 1 mL), and watch the video for the jar's water on the line while the marker last moved.
reset_notes: Stand the jar and the hose end in their trays, top the water up to 6 cm above the table with both side by side, coil the hose between the trays, dry the table, and slide the marker down to 9.2 cm. Run with -E object_jitter=0 (one fixed layout).
fidelity: The water is a model (levelhose), not particles: one surface height holding a fixed volume, found every step from the jar's and the tube's poses, with instant re-leveling (a real short level settles in about a second); a mouth below the water overflows at the Torricelli rate and what runs out is gone. The hose is drawn, not a body. The jar weighs 150 g in the sim against about 0.5 kg for a real 1 L jar holding 0.4 L of water.
